name: Search
description: A search landmark holding a labeled search field and a submit button. Use it for site or page search, and for controls that filter a list.
summary: Labeled search field and button in a landmark

elements.name: Label
elements.description: Names the field; may be visually hidden when the button makes the purpose clear

elements.name: Search field
elements.description: <input type="search">; browsers may add a clear control

elements.name: Submit button
elements.description: Runs the search; text or an icon with an accessible name

elements.name: Suggestions
elements.description: Popup list of suggested queries; turns the field into a Combobox

configOptions.options: Off, Behind a button that reveals the field

variants.caption: Full width — visible label above the field
Icon only — submit button with an icon
variants.htmlOutline:
<search>
  <form action="/search">
    <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search">
    <button aria-label="Search">
      <svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
    </button>
  </form>
</search>

variants.caption: Compact — inside the Header
variants.htmlOutline:
<header>
  …
  <search>
    <form action="/search">
      <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search site">
      <button aria-label="Search"><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
    </form>
  </search>
</header>

variants.caption: Collapsed — a button reveals the field
variants.htmlOutline:
<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="site-search" aria-label="Search">
  <svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
</button>
<search id="site-search" hidden>
  <form action="/search">
    <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search site">
    <button aria-label="Search"><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
  </form>
</search>

usageNotes: Wrap the form in <search> so it is exposed as a search landmark. For browsers without <search> support, use <form role="search"> instead.
Every search field needs a label. A visually hidden <label> is fine when the button makes the purpose clear, but placeholder text is not a label (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2).
An icon-only submit button needs an accessible name such as "Search", given with Visually hidden text or aria-label.
The landmark is for the search controls, not the results. Show results in Main. If a page has more than one search landmark, give each an aria-label so they can be told apart.
If the field shows suggestions as you type, it becomes a Combobox and should follow the ARIA Authoring Practices combobox pattern.
